Empower Federal Credit Union Amphitheater at Lakeview
shows.note: ⛈️ Show cut short by storms — Trey announced during Blaze On that the weather wasn't passing through. No encore. Stay safe, Syracuse.
🕰️ Night 1 of the MSG '92–'96 retrospective — a full 1992-era setlist, Trey in the sleeveless black.
🕰️ The '93 night of the retrospective — Phish's 93rd MSG show, played like 1993 (Trey in the Marvin the Martian shirt).
🕰️ The '94 night — a Madison Square Garden Tweezerfest nodding to 5/7/94 at the Bomb Factory: Tweezer surfacing six times before the Reprise encore.

🎸 The '95 night — and the one that finally played the song this site is named after: The Curtain ... With opened Set 2. Trey spent half the night behind a mini drum kit, and Johnny B. Goode came back after 927 shows.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: After a string of post-Sigma Oasis versions that were mostly compact, it seems the band is ready to stretch "Mercury" out again, underscored by this being the longest version since 2019. Mellow and brooding at first, the tempo rises and by 12:00, it's a perfect beach jam. The band builds towards a peak, but never quite reaches the summit. There's a fun section at the end where Trey seems like he wants to wind things down and Fish barrels through the stop sign, leading to a another couple minutes of jamming, which eventually gives way to > "Boogie On Reggae Woman".

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: Every time you wonder what "Ruby Waves" has left to say you get a version like this. Building upon loops and a driving riff, Trey leads the band into an uplifting peaking jam that hits the summit at 1630 via aggressive chord swells, only to find another gear and peaking with swirling madness some two minutes later. Akin to the Mexico 2024 "CDT" there's a relentlessness to this jam that rewards repeat spins. Dig the 8/30/24 "Ruby" call back as Trey pushes through Fishman's return to the song, aligning with bizarre alien invasion tones from Page and Mike, and launching this jam into the ether. Spellbinding stuff, sometimes the band is just so locked in. Breaking down around 26min we fade out via drones into "Lonely Trip."

tags.notes: After a somewhat anemic and imperfect composed section, "My Friend, My Friend" launches into extended improvisation yet again. Grimy murk-rock takes center stage initially, before amorphously gliding into a more melodic, patient low key psychedelic rock passage. This then morphs into the final act: a patiently wound up, somewhat mellow bliss-rock segment with melodious, laser-tone Trey guitar peaks. Longest version to date.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: It may already be cliched to observe the band is relaxed on the beach, but this very "soundchecky" outing is truly not in a hurry to get anywhere at all in particular, loping along nonchalantly for more than twenty minutes before it, almost as an afterthought, takes a turn for the funky and intergalactic. Pedal play ensues, intensity increases, and an effect infused, rocket powered dance party breaks out that finally gives way to a big melodic launch and gnarly peak that grinds and dissolves to -> BASOS.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: As if inspired by the massive reading of "A Song I Heard the Ocean Sing" that preceded it, this take spreads itself out at a luxuriating, gradual pace. Melodic and rhythmic elasticity mercurially envelop the music, as is custom for "Sea of Stars", particularly colored by Fishman's finesse-driven rhythmic flux as well as Trey's both clean and affected textural playing. Play then forms up behind a spaced-out minor key drive, sounding almost threateningly similar to "ASIHTOS", building up to smokey, hazy peak before > "Meatstick".

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: A swift pivot from the standard towards upbeat, blissful play opens the portal before shifting towards introspective melodic minor key territory. Page's dominating presence via both electric piano and wobbly synths then coaxes the jam towards psychedelia, as Fishman's tribalistic rhythms grow a bit more complex, gradually coalescing into a thick psychedelic groove-fest. After the 13:00 mark, the music puddles into an almost hellishly dense/atonal soundscape, eventually forming up into a driving attack before once again oscillating back towards soundscape-y madness. One last push for a full band groove eventually fades back into "Light's" chorus to end.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: Bliss-rock at the front gives way for more assertive, rocking play before a series of modulations begins a push and pull between major and minor key tonalities. Settling towards a funky rock zone, the band finds stability and turns the jam into am ebullient, funk-rock rave-up with a smidge of space-y ooze along the edges. This then drives towards a verve-filled peak rock section before concluding with "SYSF's" closing chorus.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: The jam vehicle of the mid-2020s drives forward in a thick groove space right out of the gates. At 10:20 Trey moves into a rawk space before sliding into a Page/Trey duel that brings back memories of Fall 2021 Phish. Trey's chordal bursts at 16:15 push the jam into a new direction before building to a heroic peak. This then fades off into a sprawling guitar-led psych jam before resolving into rhythmic WOOs. Hinting at a return to the song's chorus, Trey instead pushes the band into a swirl of noise that resolves in Piper.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: A true slow build Piper, the jam builds like all Pipers do before locking in around a Trey and Fishman duel. A chordal peaking jam, this never strays too far from what Piper does best, but it's worth hearing all the same.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: Swampy murk-rock typical of "ASIHTOS" gives way to a patient, dreamy vibe at the 5:00 mark before quickly pivoting back towards psychedelic minor-key space rock. The band holds tight here as the music blooms inward, highlighting a loose but but directional vibe. The jam then threatens a full-on funk-off, but instead spaces out around Page's clavinet and Trey's alternating wah leads and clean comping. Play then finally fades out for a > "A Wave of Hope".

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: A laid-back opening then turns briefly darker for a minute around 11:00, after which the intensity picks up and the jam crests with a powerfully sustained peak, and finally washes away in a disconcerting ambient deconstruction which eventually > "Caspian".

tags.name: Lore
tags.notes: The scene began by looking out at Las Vegas and the Sphere. Turning upside down and zooming in on a "Phish Hotel," the view passed through the peephole of the front door and into a surreal museum and library filled with odd sculptures, flying bowling pins, and toilets. After passing through several rooms, the view reached a door which opened and closed to reveal a variety of scenes, until finally backing out of the museum and returning to the Las Vegas strip.

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes:
Standard "Jim" play begins to hint at something more as Trey briefly abstracts his tone
with effects towards the front of the jam. As the harmonic range opens up a bit, a 
downshift just before the 9:00 mark takes the jam into a murky zone. Fishman's
skittering rhythms underpin an almost futuristic vibe, with Page and Mike's synth-y 
slathers grounding Trey's echo-rock lead play. Patiently working back towards major
key, the jam then finds its way back to "Jim's" traditional ending.

songs.title: Stealing Time From the Faulty Plan

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes:
Trey's relaxed comping immediately sets the tone of the jam from the onset,
establishing a hazy low-key vibe. Mike then introduces a tonal pivot towards minor key
territory which platforms a harmonically-rich and at times sci-fi textured atmosphere.
As Page moves to the piano, more organic/clean play takes shape, eventually 
modulating towards uplifting major-key heroics. This then quickly winds down to a 
low-boil and > "Plasma".

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: > from a "Seven Below" you'll want to check out. Clearly comfortable in the venue on the penultimate night of their run, the band drops "Plasma" in the two-hole of a four song suite lasting around an hour. The band toys with effects as the jam flows along effortlessly before > into a massive "C&P".

tags.name: Jamcharts
tags.notes: Emerging from the song proper into a melodic take on the main Crosseyed riff thus setting the table with an emotional build. HEROIC riff from Trey around 840 channels Eno's St Elmo's Fire. We shift around 12:25 into an overdrive rock jam before fading back into an minimalistic groove. The return to the Crosseyed chorus is dominated by increasingly demented takes on the lyrics before sonar riffs from Trey over a driving beat queues up the Phish Krautrock segment of the Sphere residency. Fade out on a demented Crosseyed riff and on perhaps the most exciting jam of the final weekend.

tags.notes: Trey announces early end to show due to weather
tags.transcript: TREY: Hey everybody, I'm gonna tell you something right while we're playing here. Very strange thing just happened in my ears, which I was told that we have to stop at a certain time - it's not yet - but it's earlier than we normally stop, so we're not gonna do an encore or anything, we're just gonna go right until they stop us, but uh, 'cuz of the weather, unfortunately, the storm is not passing through, so we're gonna play until they stop us, but trust me, it's not us stopping, it's them telling us we have to stop. Thanks for understanding.

tags.name: Narration
tags.notes: Trey explains the Vibration of Life
tags.transcript: TREY: Ladies and gentlemen, before we go any further, I just want to make sure everyone's in tune for the rest of the night. There's a special thing that we like to do here, in the Phish from Vermont. Right now we are beginning to saturate all of you with a little thing we call the Vibration of Life. If you close your eyes and concentrate, you'll start to feel a tingling in your inner sanctum and that's how you know it's working. And when Fish brings the hi-hat down, you're really gonna feel the Vibration of Life tickling your inner sanctum.
